instruction: Change the font of the document title to Arial.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully selected the '2' character in 'H2O' title and applied subscript formatting via Format > Text > Subscript menu, then saved the document. Completed in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select specific characters in LibreOffice Writer, navigate Format menu, apply text formatting (subscript), save documents
metadata.task_rationale: The model demonstrated font/formatting manipulation skills. This variation tests changing the font family of the title, requiring similar selection and formatting operations.
metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting the title and changing its font to Arial. Getter reads the docx file and extracts font names from all runs in the title paragraph (index 1). Metric checks if all runs use Arial (case-insensitive), with partial credit proportional to matching runs.

scoring_breakdown.font_change: 1.0 - All title runs use Arial font (partial credit: matching_runs / total_runs)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly opens the docx file and extracts font names from all runs in the title paragraph (index 1), which is appropriate for this document.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_font'), not expected.get('rules').
Case-insensitive font comparison is appropriate and robust.
Partial credit via matching_runs/total_runs ratio is a reasonable scoring approach.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.

Minor concern: run.font.name returns None when font is inherited from paragraph/character style rather than set explicitly on the run. The getter skips None fonts, which could lead to an empty fonts list (returning 0.0) if all runs inherit the font from style rather than having it set directly. In practice, changing font via UI typically sets it explicitly on runs, so this is unlikely to be a problem.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also checking the paragraph style's font (title_para.style.font.name) as a fallback when individual run fonts are None, to handle cases where font is set at the style level rather than the run level.
